application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A TypeScript HTTP client library built on the fetch API, providing a wrapper with JSON handling, retries, timeouts, hooks, error normalization, and Node.js support.
application.purpose: Simplify making HTTP requests and handling responses, errors, and retries across browser and Node.js environments.

domains.name: HTTP Client
domains.description: Construction and execution of HTTP requests via a fetch-based wrapper with option resolution, body serialization, and response parsing.

domains.name: Error Handling and Retry
domains.description: Normalization of failed requests into rich errors, plus retry logic for transient failures and abort/timeout handling.

domains.name: Request Lifecycle Hooks
domains.description: Extension points invoked around request, response, and error stages.

domains.name: Runtime Integration
domains.description: Selection of global or Node.js fetch implementations, header and abort controller wiring, and optional keep-alive agents.

applicationFacts: The library exports $fetch and ofetch as the primary client entry points, created via createFetch.
createFetch's internal $fetchRaw orchestrates option resolution, hooks, body serialization, timeout via AbortController, fetch invocation, response parsing, and error routing.

Retry behavior: retries are attempted for configured or default status codes (408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504) unless the request was an active abort; default retry count is 0 for payload methods and 1 otherwise.
Errors with status 400 to 599 trigger onError unless ignoreResponseError is set.

The static call graph shows createFetch calling resolveFetchOptions, callHooks, isPayloadMethod, isJSONSerializable, detectResponseType, and onError; onError calls isPayloadMethod and createFetchError.
Response bodies are parsed by default using destr for JSON responses.
The build config produces entries for src/index and src/node, with undici treated as external.
Node.js keep-alive agents are enabled only when the FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE environment variable parses to true.
unknowns: The static graph does not show the call from onError to $fetchRaw, which the source does contain; the relationship set is taken as provided by the deterministic graph.
The static graph does not include calls to external libraries such as destr, ufo, or fetch itself, so their roles are inferred from imports only.
The business context of the application beyond being an HTTP client library is not stated in the source.
Whether the example endpoint and playground endpoints are representative of intended usage is unclear.
